about: Dom 2026-10-26 (after /physics1 on his iPhone: five ragdolls + a cut, 0.40 ms a frame): the opponent's body is a physics ragdoll (@frankendom/physics, Jolt WASM, package.json) for PRESENTATION only. The 60 Hz sim (src/fight/duel.ts) and Gate 0 never see it, and nothing it does goes back into the sim. src/fight/ragdoll.ts reads every number and name here. `on`: default on; `?<query>=<v1>` (?physics=v1) = today's death and hit behaviour exactly (the chunk is never fetched). `opponents`: the opponent ids that get a ragdoll, each with the body stem it is drawn in on the 65 rig (src/assets/<body>.glb) and its body measure row per rig (`measure`: rig -> a site path the build copies from the package's data/bodies/, fetched with the chunk; the 106 body, data/rig.json files[body], has its own row from Physics Dev (physics 6ab3c99: minotaur-106.measure.json, 1.7225 m); a rig with no row gets no ragdoll and keeps today's death). `bones`: the package's 20 part ids -> the 65-rig bone names; on a 106 body each goes through data/rig.json `bones` (src/fight/rig-bones.ts bone()), the one 65 -> 106 map, never a second copy. `tickHz` / `maxTicksPerFrame`: the fixed physics step in the scene's own accumulator, beside the sim's. `seed`: the physics world's seed (the engine draws nothing; kept for the package's rand()). `loadAfterFirstFrameMs`: the chunk is imported this long after the first frame, so it never competes with the first visit. `hit`: a landed blow (sim event Hit, the opponent the target) -> the part its location strikes, the impulse (N s) along the attacker's facing plus `lift` up, and the package's stagger (rd.stagger, run on `states.stagger`). `motorTuning`: the package's per-role tracking gain and damping multipliers (keys all < role < part id): 2 / 0.25 for the body (Physics Dev's start), 1 / 1 for the neck and head, which were under-damped at 0.25 on the real clips (#56: settled long-axis median 13.3 deg at 2 / 0.25 vs 3.3 at 1 / 1). `solveHinges`: setTargetPose twists the upper arm / thigh about its long axis so the elbow / knee bend plane matches the clip (physics#14; false = the hinge as built). True (2026-10-26, physics a382384 with the left elbow's hinge sign fixed; measured on the 106 Minotaur's real clips, Mac M5, 15 s of fight each, bone direction = local +Y): on, the forearm / hand direction error is 17.3 / 21.7 deg live median (10.1 / 11.0 settled) against 41.9 / 41.8 off; the upper arm's direction is unchanged (16.0 vs 16.1) and its extra full-angle error (38.6 vs 21.1) is roll about the bone, which the stills do not show as a twist on the skin. (#58 had it off: its 'long axis' column used local X, which on these rigs is across the bone, so it counted that roll as direction.) `states`: passed to createPhysics, over the package's data/states.json key by key: `stagger` (Physics Dev's brief: arm 0.9 / forearm 0.6 / hand 0.12, the rest at the torso's 0.6, eased in 0.05 s, held 0.5 s, back over 0.35 s) and `death` (the package's own values: 1 -> 0.01 over 1 s, limp damper 2, sleeps under 0.02 m2/s2 for 4 ticks). `blend`: per part, the share of the ragdoll's pose the bones show at the dip's deepest (the dip's own shape); an unlisted part shows the clip. The spine shows fully, the neck and head half, the arms not yet. On the 106 Minotaur with physics a382384 (2026-10-26: the left-elbow hinge sign fixed, solveHinges on) the forearm and hand follow the clip's direction within 17 / 22 deg live median (10 / 11 settled), but a first try at 0.3 on the arms drew a mid-swing cleaver arm well down from the clip in the stills; the arm share is a follow-up with paired stills. Before that fix the arms were 40-45 deg off and any share flung them. `kill`: the killing blow (sim event Killed): the capsules snap onto the killing frame's pose (rd.snapToTarget), then the part by location takes the impulse along the attacker's facing plus `lift`, the death ramp runs and the bones follow the ragdoll until it sleeps; the corpse stays down until the rematch (rd.reset). `blendInS`: seconds from the clip's pose to the ragdoll's after the kill; 0 since the snap (no pop measured at 0/2/4 ticks). `finisher`: what a ragdolled opponent's kill does with the finisher rotation, `default` unless `?<query>=<a key of values>`. `keep` (?ragdoll=finishers): a cinematic finisher (Split Crown, Decapitation, Run Through, Opened) plays exactly as before and gets no ragdoll; only the plain death (the rotation's no-ceremony outcome, about 1 blade kill in 5, and every kick and skill kill) falls as a ragdoll. `skip` (the default since 2026-10-26, Dom: let's get this always on; ?ragdoll=always too): every death of his is the plain death and falls as a ragdoll; the finisher (picture and its death cue) is skipped for that kill.

cut.about: M5 cuts (physics f38dba0, docs/API.md 'Cuts (M5)'), PRESENTATION ONLY like the rest of this file (the sim and Gate 0 never see a cut; ?physics=v1 = no ragdoll, so no cut and no tap). `on`: false = no cut at all. `log`: the page's list of sim-side-presentation cut events ({ type: 'cut', unit, gear, source }), read by Strategy's loot screen later (globalThis[log]; one fight's cuts, emptied on the rematch). `onKill`: the sim's Killed.location -> the unit that leaves with that killing blow (a head-zone kill takes the head). `sever`: the unit V1's decapitation finisher takes (?ragdoll=finishers: V1's flying head stays the picture; the package's cut is made too, for its event and gear). `kill`: that cut's push, along the killing blow's facing (impulse N s, lift up). `tap`: the corpse tap (the butcher's table): a tap (no more than maxMovePx of drag and maxMs long, so the camera drag never cuts) on the corpse once the ragdoll is `needs` (frozen) raycasts the skinned body, takes the heaviest bone of the face it meets, and cuts the first unit of `order` whose bone it hangs under (the package's cut_role bones: head, an arm, a leg, then the torso at the waist, which carries everything above); `impulse` / `lift`: the piece's push along the tap's ray. `seam`: how the skinned body is split (src/fight/cut-pieces.ts): a triangle goes with the piece when the carried bones hold at least `piece` of its weight (the rule characters.ts sever() bakes the finisher's head with), and stays on the body only when no vertex of it has `bodyKeepBelow` of its weight carried (a triangle across the cut belongs to neither: the cap covers the seam). `cap`: the two stump caps (plain balls until Physics Dev's real cut-piece meshes land) (the body's, on the parent part, and the piece's, on the severed part): colour, and radiusMult times the cut part's capsule radius. `helmet`: the rigid helmet prop's placeholder mesh (only an opponent row with helmet: true gets one; the Minotaur wears none, no armour until beta). The world steps while the package's `rd.awake` says a body of the ragdoll is awake (a frozen corpse is not; the piece a cut wakes is): physics 4c708f7 replaced the page's `settleS` timer. The package's three-rig applyPose places every cut bone on its capsule's joint.

cue.about: Dom 2026-10-27 (phone test: no head came off, he did not know where to tap): once the corpse is frozen (cut.tap.needs) for delayS seconds, a pulsing round button labelled by `labels` sits on each unit of `units` that is still on it (a unit's cut bone on screen); a tap on it cuts that unit (the same push as a corpse tap). Presentation only, nothing is sent to the sim.

finisherCuts.about: Strategy's ruling (2026-10-26): V3's finishers become PHYSICS cuts + ragdoll, keeping V1's camera, blood and sound timing rows (the kill cam stays). They play under ?ragdoll=finishers (finisher mode 'physics'): the rotation picks as in V1, the scene plays the finisher's own camera, blood and sound by its id from src/fight/finisher-defs.json, and the victim's body is the ragdoll with the cut below instead of V1's victim clip. The default (finisher 'skip') is unchanged: every death the plain ragdoll death. ?ragdoll=clips = V1's cinematic finishers with V1's victim clips and no ragdoll (the old 'keep'); ?physics=v1 = V1 as it was. PRESENTATION ONLY (the sim and Gate 0 never see it). `rows`: one per finisher id of finisher-defs.json that has a physics body (a finisher with no row, such as Hamstrung and Execution, keeps its clips). `unit`: the package's cut unit (head, arm_left, arm_right, leg_left, leg_right, torso_waist) that leaves the body, or null = no cut (the blade stays through the body). `atS`: seconds after the killing blow the cut is made (0 = with the kill, as the head-zone kill's). `push`: a multiplier on kill.impulse (0.25 = the body sags and the stuck blade holds it up). `kill`: the cut piece's push {impulse, lift}, null = cut.kill. The camera, blood and sound are the finisher's own rows in finisher-defs.json, by the same id (nothing here re-states them: the kill cam is V1's, unchanged). `plane`: what V1's finisher does that the unit only stands in for (null = the unit is the cut), for Strategy to rule on a new cut plane.

splitCrown.plane: a vertical split of the head and trunk (V1's Split Crown cleaves the skull down to the chest); the head cut stands in for it until the package has a sagittal plane

opened.plane: a belly opening (V1's Opened is a cut across the belly that spills the guts with the halves held together by the spine); torso_waist severs the whole trunk at the waist, which is V1's baked waist cut
